# Pcg64Dxsm

pub struct Pcg64Dxsm {
    // private fields

## Associated functions

<h3 id="with-stream"><code>WithStream</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WithStream(seed: uint64, stream: uint64) -> Pcg64Dxsm
```

A generator on the stream `stream` selects.
Two generators with the same seed and different streams produce unrelated sequences of the same period,
which is how independent parallel streams are made without the workers having to agree on anything but
their own index.

| Name     | Type     | Description                                                 |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seed`   | `uint64` | the value the generator starts from                         |
| `stream` | `uint64` | which of the generator's independent sequences to draw from |

**Returns**: a generator seeded with that value, on the given stream

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Pcg64.rux#L44)

## Implements RandomGenerator

`Pcg64Dxsm` conforms to [`RandomGenerator`](/docs/api/random/random-generator).

<h3 id="next-uint64"><code>NextUint64</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NextUint64(self: &var Pcg64Dxsm) -> uint64
```

The next word.
The output is computed from the state before it advances. The high half is folded twice and then
multiplied by the low half forced odd — an odd multiplier is invertible, so that last step permutes the
value rather than collapsing any of it.

**Returns**: the next 64 bits

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Pcg64.rux#L78)

The multiplier used by both the state step and the output function.
PCG's "cheap" 64-bit multiplier, which the DXSM variant uses in the 128-bit step as well.

<h3 id="pcg-from-entropy"><code>PcgFromEntropy</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PcgFromEntropy() -> Pcg64Dxsm ! EntropyError
```

A [`Pcg64Dxsm`](/docs/api/random/pcg64-dxsm) seeded from the operating system's entropy, on the default stream.
Fails and recovers exactly as [`XoshiroFromEntropy`](/docs/api/random/xoshiro256#xoshiro-from-entropy) does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Seeding.rux#L26)

**Returns**: a generator seeded from the system, or why it could not be seeded

<h3 id="pcg-from-entropy-with-stream"><code>PcgFromEntropyWithStream</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PcgFromEntropyWithStream(stream: uint64) -> Pcg64Dxsm ! EntropyError
```

A [`Pcg64Dxsm`](/docs/api/random/pcg64-dxsm) seeded from entropy on the stream `stream` selects.
The intended shape for parallel work: every worker calls this with its own index, so the streams are
independent by construction and the whole run is reproducible from the one seed if it is recorded.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Seeding.rux#L36)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type     | Description                                                 |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stream` | `uint64` | which of the generator's independent sequences to draw from |

**Returns**: a generator on that stream seeded from the system, or why it could not be seeded
